tagline: Digital workflows to transform the way people work
hero_kpi_rationale: The cloud backlog (RPO) is the leading indicator of future revenue at ServiceNow, reflecting enterprise confidence in its automation platform and its ability to capitalize on the AI wave through multi-year contracts.
company_description: ServiceNow, Inc. provides cloud-based solution for digital workflows in the North America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Asia Pacific, and internationally. The company provides asset management, integrated risk management, IT service management, Operational Technology management, Security Operations, strategic portfolio management, IT operations management products; customer service management product; field service management applications; and sales and order management services. It also offers human resources delivery; legal and contract operations; workplace service delivery products; app engine product; automation engine; platform privacy and security product; and source-to-pay operations. In addition, the company provides RaptorDB, a database built to manage workloads at scale; ServiceNow Impact that provides customers with software tools, guided plans, and AI-driven recommendations; customer support; and workflow data fabric. It serves government, financial services, healthcare and life science, manufacturing, Public Sector, retail, technology, and Telecom sectors through service providers and resale partners. The company has a strategic collaboration with Cohesity, Inc

kpis.name: Cloud Backlog (cRPO)
kpis.explanation: Amount of future contractual revenue not yet recognized, to be recognized in the next 12 months.
kpis.description: cRPO (Current Remaining Performance Obligations) reached 46% of total RPO, or $12.972 billion, up 25% year-over-year.
kpis.signal: Solid growth of the short-term backlog, sign of sustained demand.

kpis.name: Remaining Performance Obligations
kpis.explanation: Total future contractual revenue not yet recognized, including non-cancelable unbilled amounts.
kpis.description: Total RPO includes deferred revenue and non-cancelable future amounts, reflecting medium-term revenue visibility.
kpis.signal: RPO at $28.2 billion, growth of 27%: strong signal of commercial traction.

kpis.name: Customers >$5M Annual Value
kpis.explanation: Number of customers generating more than $5 million in annual revenue.
kpis.description: The number of high-ACV customers rose from 502 in 2024 to 603 in 2025, up 20%, showing strong adoption in large enterprises.
kpis.signal: 603 customers >$5M: evidence of penetration in large accounts.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and service cost, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin remains high, consistent with the low-variable-cost SaaS model.
kpis.signal: High gross margin typical of cloud software vendors.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin is expanding thanks to efficiency gains and scale.

kpis.name: R&D (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses divided by revenue.
kpis.description: ServiceNow maintains a high R&D rate, consistent with its strategy of continuous innovation on the AI platform.
kpis.signal: High investment in innovation, notably in AI.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on physical or digital assets to support growth.
kpis.description: Investments are rising to support platform infrastructure and AI integration.
kpis.signal: Capex rising to strengthen cloud infrastructure.

kpis.name: Headcount (Employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees at the company.
kpis.description: Headcount rose to 18,500 employees, up 8%, mainly in sales and engineering.
kpis.signal: Headcount growth to support commercial expansion.

kpis.name: Subscription Revenue
kpis.explanation: Measures ServiceNow's annual recurring subscription revenue from software, a key financial health indicator.

kpis.name: Subscription Growth (constant currency)
kpis.explanation: Measures subscription revenue growth excluding FX changes to show true commercial performance.

kpis.name: FCF Margin
kpis.explanation: Measures the percentage of cash generated after investments. Indicates whether ServiceNow is truly creating wealth.

kpis.name: Renewal Rate
kpis.explanation: Measures the percentage of customers who renew their ServiceNow subscription, indicating customer satisfaction and loyalty.

risks.title: Data Regulations Hinder Optimization
risks.summary: Data protection and digital sovereignty laws limit our ability to optimize the platform and to operate in certain countries.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned at the top of the risk section, mention of restrictions on data use, storage and transfer, with reference to constraining regulations such as the EU Data Regulation and the Transatlantic framework. Strong language on operational and geographic impact. Regulation category heavily weighted.

risks.title: Failure to Innovate in Face of Technology Competition
risks.summary: The inability to keep up with the rapid pace of technology innovation, particularly in AI, could weaken our competitive position.
risks.score_rationale: Alarming language about the speed of innovation, native AI, automation and increased competition. Existential risk emphasized by the threat of losing market share, margins and customer acceptance. Central position in the document.

risks.title: AI Integration as a Source of Legal and Ethical Risks
risks.summary: Accelerated AI integration exposes the company to poorly mastered regulatory, ethical and competitive risks.
risks.score_rationale: Repeated mention of operational, regulatory and ethical challenges related to AI, with explicit reference to the EU AI Act. Growing risk specifically highlighted as strategic. Technology category strongly impacted.

risks.title: Cybersecurity: Real or Perceived Breaches
risks.summary: Any security breach, real or perceived, at us or our service providers, could seriously damage our reputation and revenue.
risks.score_rationale: Presented as a major risk potentially leading to customer losses, lawsuits and reputational damage. Strong language on the perception of insecurity. High position in the operational section.

risks.title: Growing Dependence on Partners for Revenue
risks.summary: Our growth increasingly depends on partners whose failure to deliver could harm our results and customer relationships.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of increased dependence on partners for revenue. Direct operational risk if partners fail. Secondary position but reinforced by the complex sales context.

risks.title: International Expansion Difficulties
risks.summary: International expansion is expensive and complex, with high regulatory, economic and operational risks in new markets.
risks.score_rationale: 37% of revenue outside North America, but repeated regulatory, cultural and operational obstacles. Heavy investments with no guaranteed return. Strategic risk for growth.

risks.title: Loss of Key Talent or Recruitment Difficulties
risks.summary: The loss of key management members or technical talent could hinder our ability to innovate and execute our strategy.
risks.score_rationale: Direct mention in operational risks, with a link to innovation and growth capacity. Concerned language about talent retention. Key-person category critical in tech.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence was found in the text.
